claim: The ToxASCII benchmark (7,046 samples) achieved a 1.00 attack success rate against Perspective API, OpenAI Omni-Moderation, and Llama Guard 3, because none interpret spatially-structured (ASCII-art) text.
Under homoglyph attack, OpenAI Moderation accuracy fell to 50.77% and Perspective API fell from 94.28% to 64.84%; perturbed-text accuracy dropped ~25 points even for trained classifiers.
Validated TaeBench adversarial toxic examples achieved attack success rate 77.22% vs Llama Guard, 36.41% vs OpenAI Moderation, 36.20% vs Detoxify, but only 8.94% vs the multi-stage NeMo Guardrails.

A Regex to CPU to GPU moderation cascade used a sub-0.2ms regex stage to resolve 18% of traffic for free; deterministic regex filters suit syntactically-fixed patterns at sub-millisecond latency, learned stages suit semantic/obfuscated variation.
Llama Guard scored 0.626 AUPRC on ToxicChat versus OpenAI API 0.588 and Perspective 0.532, and matched OpenAI zero-shot on its own dataset (0.847 vs 0.856).
Constitutional Classifiers survived over 3,000 red-team hours with no universal jailbreak, at a cost of only +0.38% production refusals and 23.7% inference overhead.
Across a six-dimension Oogiri humor rubric, LLM-judge agreement with humans on overall funniness topped out at Spearman rho 0.266, with LLMs optimizing novelty while humans weight empathy.
HumorRank, a Bradley-Terry pairwise humor leaderboard, reports human-human agreement of Krippendorff alpha 0.397 and only about 49% LLM-judge alignment with humans.
The CALM benchmark quantifies 12 systematic LLM-as-judge biases including verbosity, position, and self-enhancement, with position-bias robustness as low as 0.566.
G-Eval shows BLEU and ROUGE correlate poorly with human judgment on creative tasks; chain-of-thought GPT-4 scoring reaches Spearman correlation only about 0.514 on summarization.
Syntactic-template and n-gram-based creativity metrics are ineffective in settings dominated by formulaic language and disagree across domains; unique n-grams do not equal idea originality.
A Panel of LLM evaluators of three smaller cross-family models raised human agreement to Cohen's kappa 0.763 versus 0.627 for a single GPT-4 judge on Natural Questions, at 7-8x lower cost.
Nine LLM judges drawn from seven families behave like only about 2.2 effective independent voters because of correlated errors, and aggregation closes at most about 11% of the accuracy gap.
The Wald normal-approximation confidence interval for a binomial proportion has erratic and poor coverage even at large n; the Wilson score interval is recommended for small samples.

Regression testing of non-deterministic AI workflows should use three-valued PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE verdicts from a confidence test, and SPRT cuts the trials needed by about 78% versus fixed-N while preserving Type I/II error bounds.
An SPRT calibrated to an LLM's output distribution terminates self-consistency sampling early, matching fixed-N (typically 40-64 samples) accuracy at substantially lower token cost.
Temperature-zero greedy LLM decoding is not deterministic: batch-size-dependent floating-point reduction order flips tokens run-to-run, so exact-match golden tests on generated text remain flaky.
LLM refusal and safety behavior is unstable across random seeds and temperature, so single-sample safety evaluation can both miss vulnerabilities and overstate safety.
Trust calibration is appropriate reliance matched to the automation's actual reliability in the local context; a trust signal that does not track real reliability produces mis-calibrated reliance.
AI explanations and outputs increase the chance a human accepts the recommendation regardless of correctness, and confidence scores alone are insufficient to achieve complementary team performance.

First-person uncertainty expression by an LLM significantly reduced inappropriate agreement and overreliance and raised accuracy, while general or passive phrasing had weaker, non-significant effects.
Cognitive forcing functions reduced overreliance on AI more than plain explanations did, but participants rated the friction-heavy designs least favorably.

Mixed-initiative systems should weigh the expected cost and benefit of acting under uncertainty and provide a fallback safety net, scoping autonomous action to the uncertainty rather than acting all-or-nothing.
